absent: Numeric values of state flags, trigger codes and error codes beyond success versus failure distinctions.
Conditions that make vector management report busy and full direct affinity programming path.
Resend tasklet body, resend list initialization, and who drains queued descriptors.
Chip operation bodies for enable, disable, mask, unmask, shutdown, startup, ack, eoi and set type.
Autoprobe start path, probing mutex acquisition, and IRQ_GET_DESC_CHECK_GLOBAL semantics.
Domain activation and hierarchical parent linkage setup and teardown details.
Effective affinity computation and single target determination.
Power core wakeup notification effects and suspend resume interaction.
Proc display layout and sparse tree lookup and locking beyond insertion.
Threaded handler wake queue setup and spurious interrupt debug accounting.

findings.text: Affinity setup leaves per CPU and non balanceable lines untouched and otherwise chooses an online target set, preferring an existing managed or user supplied choice when any of its CPUs stays online, falling back to defaults and full online membership, narrowing to the owning NUMA node when possible, with an alternate build delegating to a generic selector.

Affinity changes first attempt direct programming and when the vector layer reports busy for a non forced request the implementation records the request as pending and reports success instead of propagating busy, while a separate build without pending support propagates busy.

For hierarchy lines that expect affinity at activation time, a request arriving before activation only stores the supplied mask as current and effective affinity and marks affinity as set, without invoking the chip driver; otherwise the caller must proceed with normal programming.

Affinity change notification requires the caller to hold the descriptor lock, takes a reference on the notification object before scheduling its work item, and releases the extra reference when the work was already queued.
One affinity setup variant serializes selection of its shared temporary mask with a dedicated static raw lock, so concurrent setup calls cannot interleave mask construction.

Resend checking refuses level sensitive lines and clears their pending marker, refuses when a replay is already outstanding, succeeds trivially when nothing is pending and no injection was asked, otherwise clears pending, attempts hardware retrigger then software resend, and marks replay on success.

Software resend is unavailable when the line must run in interrupt context, redirects nested thread lines to their parent descriptor and fails when no parent exists, with an alternate build that always fails.

Queuing for software resend holds the global resend lock only while testing and inserting the descriptor link, ensuring each descriptor appears once before kicking the resend tasklet; clearing removes the link under the same lock, with a no operation variant in another build.

Retrigger prefers the descriptor chip operation when present, otherwise walks ancestor data toward the root and invokes the first ancestor that provides a retrigger operation, treating absence as benign.

Activation bypasses domain activation for managed lines, shutdown acts only when started by clearing any resend, deepening disable depth, invoking chip shutdown or generic disable while marking disabled and masked, then clearing started, and combined shutdown plus deactivation always invokes domain deactivation which is safe even without prior activation.

Disable and mask operations are idempotent: already disabled or masked state avoids redundant chip calls, disable prefers a dedicated chip disable operation and otherwise masks when asked, with unlazy configuration deciding whether public disable also masks.

Autoprobe collection walks every descriptor under its own lock, clears autodetection marking, shuts down and deactivates each probed descriptor, releases the global probing mutex, and then either builds a low line bitmask masked by the caller value or reports a single firing line with a negated value when several fired.
A chained line must never reach a threaded action handler; the placeholder handler warns once and reports no handling when this contract is violated.
The kernel provides a prebuilt chained action object whose handler member points at the placeholder that warns and reports no handling.

Chip, trigger type, handler data, chip data and message interrupt descriptor assignment are exposed as line number based setters that fail when the descriptor cannot be resolved, update common or per chip state under descriptor or bus scope, substitute a default no operation chip when cleared, record sparse allocation and track the widest chip name for proc display.

Trigger programming narrows the request to sense bits, succeeds trivially with a debug note when the chip lacks a type operation, masks the line around chips that require masked programming and restores afterwards, updates stored trigger and level markings only on accepted result codes, and logs failures.

Message interrupt association records the supplied entry on the target descriptor and when the offset is zero also records the base line number inside the entry; descriptor lookup for raw chip data returns null when the line is unknown.
Constants IRQ_STARTUP_NORMAL and IRQ_STARTUP_MANAGED and IRQ_STARTUP_ABORT identify the three startup paths.

Managed startup clears the managed shutdown marker, undoes one level of disable depth added at managed shutdown, and only performs startup with resend and start condition when depth reaches zero, preserving an explicit disable across hotplug cycles.
Per CPU enable prefers a dedicated chip enable operation and otherwise unmasks, while disable prefers chip disable and otherwise masks, each updating the per CPU enabled membership for the given CPU.

Combined mask plus acknowledge prefers a single chip operation and otherwise separates masking from acknowledgement while marking masked, and threaded unmask performs end of interrupt when the chip advertises threaded end of interrupt before unmasking.

Waiting for in progress completion on multiprocessor builds temporarily releases the descriptor lock while spinning on the in progress flag, reacquires it, and then reports whether the line stayed enabled with an action present.

Handling is allowed immediately when neither in progress nor wakeup armed is set; a wakeup armed line is handed to power management and refused; a line polled elsewhere waits for progress; otherwise only single target edge lines whose effective target is the current CPU may wait, all other busy cases are refused.

Power management wakeup handling disarms wakeup, marks suspended and pending, deepens disable depth, disables the line and notifies the power core, with a no operation variant in builds without that support.

Action gating clears replay and waiting markers, then refuses and marks pending when no action is attached or the line is disabled; overall handling requires both power management permission and action permission.

Nested interrupt entry may sleep, validates actions under the descriptor lock while accounting statistics and raising the active thread count, then invokes each thread function outside the lock, records debug information unless suppressed, and wakes waiters when the last thread completes.
Interrupt accounting increments both the descriptor per CPU counter and the global sum plus the descriptor total count for the current CPU.

Migrating a high rate edge line can leave the new target observing in progress while the old target loops on pending, so the new target busy waits for progress instead of masking and pending forever; a warning fires when polling is observed on the same CPU.

Line based setters synchronize through descriptor or bus scoped locks, sparse allocation serializes through a dedicated mutex while inserting into the sparse tree, and proc width tracking serializes through its own raw lock with interrupt state saved, with no operation replacements in some builds.

Several helpers have build dependent empty variants: pending copy, one resend clear, one proc chip update, one sparse mark and one power management wakeup do nothing, and probe permission is denied only when the no probe marking is present.
